description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 2 on t/op/eval.t:30-31).

perl: `() = LIST` is an ordinary list assignment whose left side happens to be
empty.  In LIST context it yields the LHS -- nothing.  In SCALAR context a
list assignment yields the number of elements on its RIGHT, which is the
well-known "countof" idiom `my $n = () = f()`.

PCL yields the LAST element of the RHS in both contexts.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    sub show { printf "n=%d [%s]\n", scalar(@_),
                      join("|", map { $_ // 'undef' } @_) }
    show( +()=(7,8) );              # perl  n=0 []        PCL  n=1 [8]
    show( +()=eval q{die} );        # perl  n=0 []        PCL  n=1 [undef]
    my $x = +()=(7,8);              # perl  2             PCL  8

The two spellings that COERCE explicitly are already right, which is what
locates it:

    show( scalar(()=(7,8)) );       # perl n=1 [2]        PCL n=1 [2]
    show( 0+(()=(7,8)) );           # perl n=1 [2]        PCL n=1 [2]

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/eval.t 9 `eval syntax error in list
context` and 10 `eval run-time error in list context`.  The file writes
`is +()=eval '++', 0, '...'` and PCL hands `is` an undef where perl hands it
0.  NOTE: the EVAL half of those rows is NOT the bug -- `my @r = eval { die }`
is 0 elements in PCL exactly as in perl (probes/p9.pl, all five shapes
identical), so the rows are the `()=` idiom and nothing else.

SHAPE: the emitter lowers `() = LIST` as if the LHS were absent, so the
assignment's VALUE is the RHS's last value.  A list assignment's value is a
context question the `p-list-=` family already answers for a non-empty LHS
(`my ($a,$b) = f()` in scalar context is the RHS count); the empty LHS is the
case that never reaches it.  Probe `(my @x) = (7,8)` and `(undef) = (7,8)` at
the same time -- they are the neighbours that must not move.
subject: SILENT WRONG (the `()=` COUNTOF idiom): an assignment whose LHS is the EMPTY LIST yields the LAST RHS ELEMENT instead of the count / the empty list
